symbols.description: A narrow band of strong wind and a type of air current that forms high in the atmosphere.
symbols.name: Jet stream

symbols.description: The four main jet streams associated with Earth: two polar jet streams and two subtropical jet streams.
symbols.name: Primary jet streams

symbols.description: A jet stream near one of Earth’s poles; polar jet streams can reach especially high speeds in winter.
symbols.name: Polar jet stream

symbols.description: A jet stream located closer to the equator.
symbols.name: Subtropical jet stream

symbols.description: Moving air, including the strong movement found in jet streams.
symbols.name: Wind

symbols.description: A movement of air; a jet stream is a type of air current.
symbols.name: Air current

symbols.description: A mass of warmer air that meets cooler air masses and rises higher in the atmosphere.
symbols.name: Warm air mass

symbols.description: A mass of cooler air that meets warmer air masses and sinks to replace rising warm air.
symbols.name: Cool air mass

symbols.description: The layer of air surrounding Earth in which jet streams form and in which air masses move.
symbols.name: Atmosphere

symbols.description: The planet whose atmosphere, surface, poles, equator, and jet streams are described.
symbols.name: Earth

symbols.description: The source of heating that does not warm the whole Earth evenly.
symbols.name: Sun

symbols.description: The region of Earth near which areas are hot and subtropical jet streams are located closer.
symbols.name: Equator

symbols.description: The north and south polar regions of Earth, near which areas are cold and polar jet streams are located.
symbols.name: Poles

symbols.description: The upward movement of warmer air in the atmosphere when it meets cooler air.
symbols.name: Warm-air rise

symbols.description: The downward movement of cooler air to replace warmer air that has risen.
symbols.name: Cool-air sinking

aliases: warm air masses meet cold air masses
symbols.description: The meeting of warm and cool air masses that forms jet streams and can create turbulent conditions.
symbols.name: Air-mass meeting

symbols.description: The formation of a jet stream when warm air masses meet cold air masses in the atmosphere.
symbols.name: Jet-stream formation

symbols.description: The speed at which a jet stream moves, averaging about 110 miles per hour and sometimes reaching 250 miles per hour or faster.
symbols.name: Jet-stream speed

symbols.description: The direction in which a jet stream travels or moves, generally from west to east but sometimes in different ways.
symbols.name: Jet-stream direction

symbols.description: The position of a jet stream about five to nine miles above Earth’s surface in the mid to upper troposphere.
symbols.name: Jet-stream location

symbols.description: The layer of Earth’s atmosphere where people live and breathe, including its mid to upper region where jet streams and airplanes are located.
symbols.name: Troposphere

symbols.description: An aircraft that flies in the mid to upper troposphere and can receive a boost from a jet stream when traveling in the same direction.
symbols.name: Airplane

symbols.description: An increase in an airplane’s travel advantage when it flies in the same direction as a powerful jet stream.
symbols.name: Airplane boost

symbols.description: A system of weather that jet streams can transport across the United States or that can remain in place when far from a jet stream.
symbols.name: Weather system

symbols.description: The region across which jet streams can transport weather systems.
symbols.name: United States

symbols.description: A property of air and weather that differs between warm and cool air masses and is affected by jet streams.
symbols.name: Temperature

symbols.description: A weather condition affected by weather systems transported by jet streams.
symbols.name: Precipitation

symbols.description: A period of heat that can result when a weather system remains in one place away from a jet stream.
symbols.name: Heat wave

symbols.description: A condition that can result when a weather system remains in one place away from a jet stream.
symbols.name: Flood

symbols.description: A weather event that jet streams typically move and that tends to follow the edge of a jet stream.
symbols.name: Storm

symbols.description: A bulge of winds to the north or south created when a jet stream moves in a different way from its usual west-to-east travel.
symbols.name: Jet-stream bulge

symbols.description: The edge of a jet stream that storms tend to follow.
symbols.name: Jet-stream edge

symbols.description: Conditions created where the difference between cool and warm air near the edge of a jet stream contributes to storms.
symbols.name: Turbulent conditions

symbols.description: Cold air that meets warmer and wetter air when a jet stream is pushed farther south.
symbols.name: Arctic air

symbols.description: An atmospheric phenomenon associated with the warmer and wetter air meeting colder Arctic air near a southward-pushed jet stream.
symbols.name: Thunder

symbols.description: An atmospheric phenomenon associated with the warmer and wetter air meeting colder Arctic air near a southward-pushed jet stream.
symbols.name: Lightning

symbols.description: A severe weather event associated with the warmer and wetter air meeting colder Arctic air near a southward-pushed jet stream.
symbols.name: Tornado

propositions.statement: Jet-stream speeds of 250 miles per hour or faster are greater than the average speed of about 110 miles per hour.
A jet stream transports a weather system across the United States.

relationships.statement: A jet stream is a type of air current.
A polar jet stream is a type of jet stream.
A subtropical jet stream is a type of jet stream.
The two polar jet streams are part of Earth's four primary jet streams.
The two subtropical jet streams are part of Earth's four primary jet streams.
Jet streams form high in the atmosphere.
Jet streams are located in the mid to upper troposphere.
Polar jet streams are near the north and south poles.
Subtropical jet streams are closer to the equator.
Warm air masses meet cooler air masses.
The meeting of warm and cool air masses forms jet streams.
When warm air masses meet cooler air, the warmer air rises higher in the atmosphere.
When cool air meets warm air, the cooler air sinks to replace the warm air.
Warm-air rise and cool-air sinking occur together when warm and cool air masses meet.
The movement of warmer air upward, together with cooler air sinking, creates an air current.
The movement of cooler air downward, together with warmer air rising, creates an air current.
Dramatic temperature differences between warm and cool air masses can cause jet streams to move at much higher speeds.
Jet streams affect temperature.
Jet streams affect precipitation.
Jet streams transport weather systems across the United States.
Weather systems are transported across the United States by jet streams.
A weather system that remains in one place can cause heat waves.
A weather system that remains in one place can cause floods.
Jet streams typically move storms from west to east.
Jet streams typically move weather systems from west to east.
Jet streams moving in different ways from their usual west-to-east travel create bulges of winds to the north and south.
Storms tend to follow the edge of the jet stream.
The difference between cool and warm air near the jet-stream edge creates turbulent conditions for storms.
Colder Arctic air meets warmer and wetter air near a southward-pushed jet stream.
The meeting of colder Arctic air with warmer and wetter air makes for more thunder.
The meeting of colder Arctic air with warmer and wetter air makes for more lightning.
The meeting of colder Arctic air with warmer and wetter air makes for more tornadoes.
An airplane traveling in the same direction as a powerful jet stream can get a boost.
Airplanes fly in the mid to upper troposphere.
Polar jet streams can reach especially high speeds in winter.

ACTIVE RELATIONSHIP CONTRACTS (source --TYPE--> target):
IS_A [STRUCTURAL; direction=instance_to_type]
  meaning: The source is a kind, category, or subtype of the target.
  roles: source=instance or subtype; target=broader type or category
  use: The source can truthfully be described as a target.
  avoid: Do not use for parts, examples, similarity, or temporary states.
PART_OF [STRUCTURAL; direction=part_to_whole]
  meaning: The source is a constituent or component of the target.
  roles: source=part or component; target=containing whole
  use: The source exists as a component or subpart of the target.
  avoid: Never reverse whole and part; do not use for interaction or dependency.
EXAMPLE_OF [STRUCTURAL; direction=example_to_concept]
  meaning: The source is an illustrative instance of the target concept.
  roles: source=example; target=concept illustrated
  use: The source is presented as an example of the target.
  avoid: Do not use merely because the source is a subtype; prefer IS_A for classification.
CAUSES [CAUSAL; direction=cause_to_effect]
  meaning: The source brings about the target as an effect.
  roles: source=cause; target=effect
  use: The source is stated to produce the target outcome.
  avoid: Do not use for chronology, association, contribution, or unspecified influence.
AFFECTS [CAUSAL; direction=influence_to_affected]
  meaning: The source causally influences the target without a specified direction or complete production.
  roles: source=influence; target=affected entity, process, or variable
  use: The source changes or influences the target, but the text does not support CAUSES, INCREASES, or DECREASES.
  avoid: Do not use for mere association, chronology, physical force, or interaction with no stated effect.
INCREASES [CAUSAL; direction=increaser_to_increased_variable]
  meaning: The source causally raises the amount, rate, value, probability, or intensity of the target.
  roles: source=causal factor; target=quantity or variable increased
  use: The source is explicitly said to make the target greater, faster, more likely, or more intense.
  avoid: Do not infer from nearby words such as more or faster; never use when the source says slower, lower, or less.
DECREASES [CAUSAL; direction=decreaser_to_decreased_variable]
  meaning: The source causally lowers the amount, rate, value, probability, or intensity of the target.
  roles: source=causal factor; target=quantity or variable decreased
  use: The source is explicitly said to make the target smaller, slower, less likely, or less intense.

INDUCES [CAUSAL; direction=inducer_to_induced_effect]
  meaning: The source produces the target through an explicitly described induction mechanism.

  avoid: Do not use for delivery, participation, weak assistance, or an effect that actually occurred.

  use: The source cannot operate or occur as described without the target.

  use: The source explicitly occurs before, previously, first, then, or after relative to the target.
